title: A word check inside a choice
idea: Word comparisons fit inside nested ifs too. Combine last unit's nesting with this unit's word tests. Predict the path.

exercises.explanation: signed_in is True, so enter the branch; role == "admin" is True, so the inner if prints "Admin tools".

exercises.prompt: Same code, role = "editor" (still signed in). What prints?
exercises.explanation: Signed in, but "editor" is not "admin", so the inner else runs: "User tools".

exercises.prompt: Same code, signed_in = False. What prints?
exercises.explanation: The outer gate is False, so the role check is skipped and the outer else runs: "Please sign in".

exercises.prompt: Why does checking the role go INSIDE the signed-in check?
options: The role only matters once the user is signed in
exercises.explanation: A follow-up that only matters after the first answer is settled belongs nested inside - the same nesting idea as last unit.

exercises.prompt: Build: if the door state is "open", then if the word is "vip" print "Lounge" else print "Hall"; if the door is not open, print "Closed".
exercises.explanation: Outer word test on door; inner word test on guest; outer else for a closed door. Word checks nest like any condition.

exercises.prompt: For that code with door = "open", guest = "regular", what prints?
exercises.explanation: Door open, but "regular" is not "vip", so the inner else prints "Hall".

exercises.prompt: Same code, door = "shut", guest = "vip". What prints?
exercises.explanation: "shut" is not "open", so the inner check is skipped and the outer else prints "Closed". The guest word never matters.

exercises.prompt: A word comparison can be the OUTER condition of a nested if.
exercises.explanation: Yes - door == "open" is just True/False, so it works as an outer gate exactly like a number test.

exercises.prompt: This combines two units. Which two ideas?
options: Nested if (from last unit) and word comparison (this unit)
exercises.explanation: You are layering a word test inside a nested if - the new tool slotting into the structure you already learned.

options: Word tests behave like any condition, so they fit anywhere a condition can go - including nested ifs
Words only work at the top level
You must use numbers inside nests
exercises.explanation: A condition is a condition. Word comparisons plug into ifs, elifs, and nested branches just like number comparisons.
